notes: Object insert. Years are individuals (no date comparison is needed for q0 and q1). The two worlds only differ on the oldest-certificate superlative (fol temporal), so they carry no axioms. Relations once declared in this file are catalogued in RELATIONS.md since 2026-10-30 (founded_in is founded_in_year, dissolved_in is dissolved_in_year).

queries.not_checked: fol (temporal): the oldest certificate's date (comparing dates)

fol.notes: Certificates are an enumeration (distinct by construction) with other_certificate standing for every other known VOC certificate; dated_on is the date a document bears (day number, ATTRIBUTES.md). The edit is the issued certificate with its date (part of the inserted fact). w1 stores the superlative about the Enkhuizen share (oldest_certificate, local), which the edit does not recompute; w2 stores the rule that reads it off the dates of the issued certificates. That every other known certificate is dated after 9 September 1606 is the closed-world presupposition w2's comparison rests on. Day numbers: 9 September 1606 = 586466, 3 June 1606 = 586368, September 1606 = 586458 to 586487.

local.oldest_certificate: oldest_certificate(c): the earliest-dated known share certificate company c issued (an individual, not a value)

enkhuizen_1606.says: The VOC issued the Enkhuizen share, dated 9 September 1606. (stored)

others_later.says: Every other known VOC share certificate is dated after 9 September 1606. (closed world)

enkhuizen: the Enkhuizen share of 9 September 1606 (Pieter Harmensz)
